# Field-wise row constraints

[A constraint applies an aspect bound to **every field** of a row](#spec.types.generics.field-wise-row-constraints.legality-1), rather than to the
row's own type as a whole — distinct from a row *bound* (`R: .{ .x: f64, .. }`), which
constrains the row's shape (which labels it has), not its contents (what the field
types can do):

```metel
extend<record R> .{ ..R }: Display where ..R: Display { … }
fun consume<record R>(r: .{ ..R })  where ..R: Copy     { … }
```

`..R: A` holds when every field type in `R`'s row satisfies `A`; it holds vacuously on an
empty row. A per-field exception composes through ordinary row decomposition (`where R
= { x: T, ..Rest }, T: SomeOtherBound, ..Rest: A`) rather than needing a
heterogeneous form of its own.

[The operand is `..` followed by the name of a `record` parameter](#spec.types.generics.field-wise-row-constraints.legality-1). `R: A` instead
bounds the record as a whole. A type or literal row after `..` in a bound is a
parse error; a parameter without the `record` kind is rejected with `T0012`.

[`R` must be a row the declaration can walk](#spec.types.generics.field-wise-row-constraints.legality-1): the tail of an open-row parameter
(`.{ ..R }`), the remainder of a `where` decomposition, the tail of an `extend` target
(`extend<record R> .{ ..R }`), or a declared `record` generic used as the row argument of a
named type (`Packet<..R>`), in a function signature or an `extend` target. A row that
none of these positions mentions has no fields to constrain and is rejected.

```metel
aspect Mark { fun mark(&self) -> i64; }
record Packet<record R> { data: .{ ..R } }
fun duplicate<record R>(p: Packet<..R>) -> (.{ ..R }, .{ ..R }) where ..R: Copy {
    let d := p.data;
    (d, d)
}
extend<record R> Packet<..R>: Mark where ..R: Copy { fun mark(&self) -> i64 { 1 } }

fun main() {
    let p := Packet { data = .{ .a = 1 } };
    assert(p.mark() == 1);
    let pair := duplicate(p);
    assert(pair.0.a + pair.1.a == 2);
}
```

<details>
<summary>Formal rules</summary>

##### Legality Rule {#spec.types.generics.field-wise-row-constraints.legality-1}

`where ..R: Aspect` is a `WhereConstraint` alternative, sibling to an ordinary bound
(`ident : BoundList`) and a row equation (`ident = Type`, [Open rows](open-rows.md)
above): it holds exactly when every field type in row `R` satisfies `Aspect`,
vacuously on an empty row. It constrains `R`'s field *contents*; it does not by itself
constrain which labels `R` has (that is an ordinary row bound, composed separately).
